blocks.html: Tanzania and Zanzibar in 12 days: Diamond Luxury holiday

blocks.orig: You’ve watched countless documentaries about Tanzania, and you’ve been dreaming about seeing all of this with your own eyes for a long time? However, you also love to relax and get pampered during your holiday? Then we’ve found the perfect vacation match for you! This route combines exciting adventures with luxury at its best – in our Diamond Luxury resorts.
blocks.html: Have you seen documentary after documentary about Tanzania and wanted to experience it in person for years? And do you also like to unwind and be looked after while you are away? Then this trip could be exactly what you are looking for. The route pairs thrilling adventures with top-level comfort, staying in our Diamond Luxury resorts.

blocks.orig: During these twelve days you visit the majestic Tarangire National Park and a coffee farm. Furthermore, you dive into the unique landscape of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and marvel at the endless Serengeti from a hot air balloon.
blocks.html: Over these twelve days you explore the impressive Tarangire National Park and call in at a coffee farm. You also discover the remarkable scenery of the Ngorongoro Conservation Area and take in the seemingly endless Serengeti from the basket of a hot air balloon.

blocks.orig: After all these once-in-a-lifetime experiences it’s time for a tropical paradise: relax on Zanzibar in a five-star-resort with vibes from 1001 Arabian Nights. This is what a perfect luxury holiday looks like.
blocks.html: Once you have had these unique experiences, a tropical island is waiting: unwind on Zanzibar at a five-star resort with a 1001 Arabian Nights feel. That is our idea of the ideal luxury holiday.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear a lot is when you should travel to Tanzania. Honestly, there is no single correct answer. It comes down to what you hope to see, the places you want to visit, your budget and what interests you. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to travel to Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: On a safari with us you get the chance to discover Tanzania’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is yours alone. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and our experienced guides are happy to help you decide on the day itself. Perhaps you want to see the animals when they are most active around sunrise and sunset, when it is pleasantly cool, or perhaps you would rather finish the afternoon at the pool: the choice is yours. Because animals in Tanzania are active at different times of day, you will have many chances to see them in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo can all be seen in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Yes, Tanzania is a safe and friendly country for travellers. You will find a hospitable atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, and you can enjoy the scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are welcoming, and as anywhere else in the world it is sensible to take normal precautions, such as watching your belongings. With its natural beauty and warm people, Tanzania is a wonderful country to visit.

blocks.orig: As you walk out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide greets you with a big smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' The guide takes you straight to your hotel, where you can relax and take in the African atmosphere. The next day your guide takes you on an exclusive, private safari that allows you to travel at your own pace. Enjoy the luxury of your own safari jeep and take the liberty to stop and watch the animals as long as you like!
blocks.html: When you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your personal Your Tanzania Trip guide is waiting with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. The following day your guide sets off with you on an exclusive, private safari, so you can travel at the pace that suits you. You have your own safari jeep, and you are free to stop and watch the animals for as long as you want.

blocks.orig: In the majestic Tarangire National Park, the focus lies on grandeur - cross paths with the countless gigantic baobab trees, in search of vast herds of elephants. And these giants are not the only large game you find here, since the Tarangire River and Lake Burunge attract countless lions, zebras, giraffes, leopards, cheetahs, pythons, and monkeys to their waters. For smaller species, the grandeur lies in the numbers, as Tarangire is also an absolute haven for birdwatchers!
blocks.html: Grandeur is the theme in the impressive Tarangire National Park: you pass countless enormous baobab trees while looking for large herds of elephants. They are not the only big animals here, because the Tarangire River and Lake Burunge draw many lions, zebras, giraffes, leopards, cheetahs, pythons and monkeys to the water. For the smaller species it is all about numbers, as Tarangire is a true haven for birdwatchers.

blocks.orig: Mto wa Mbu is a village close to Lake Manyara National Park, where it stands out as a green oasis in the middle of the surrounding Maasai plains. Get a taste of culture and discover this lovely little village, the surrounding lush green nature, and the banana plantations by hopping on a mountainbike. Then get off your bike to visit a nearby Maasai village, where some Maasai tribesmen tell you all about their way of life.
blocks.html: Close to Lake Manyara National Park lies the village of Mto wa Mbu, a green oasis surrounded by the Maasai plains. Jump on a mountain bike to get a feel for the local culture and explore the charming village, the lush green countryside around it and the banana plantations. Afterwards you leave the bike behind and visit a Maasai village nearby, where Maasai tribesmen explain how they live.

blocks.orig: Gibb's Farm offers the old-age rhythm of an African farm and coffee plantation, right on the slopes of Ngorongoro Highlands. Walk around on this sanctuary of peace and tranquility, and watch vegetables being harvested, coffee roasted, cows milked, and pigs fed. The vegetable gardens, fruit trees, and herbs provide inspiration for the farm's chefs, who in their turn amaze visitors with a delicious lunch. A little piece of heaven!
blocks.html: On the slopes of the Ngorongoro Highlands, Gibb's Farm follows the age-old rhythm of an African farm and coffee plantation. Stroll around this peaceful, quiet sanctuary, and see how vegetables are harvested, coffee is roasted, cows are milked and pigs are fed. The farm's chefs draw inspiration from the vegetable gardens, fruit trees and herbs, and they then treat visitors to a tasty lunch. A small slice of heaven!

blocks.orig: Today you descend into the wonderous caldera of the famous Ngorongoro Crater. This is THE day to start your game drive early when animals are plenty and tourists few! Feel the little hairs on your arms rise as you descend into the crater, awed by the sight of clouds hovering and the numerous animals in sight. Coyotes, hyenas, buffaloes, wildebeests, gazelles, and many more animals can be found here and you are almost guaranteed to see them all.
blocks.html: Today you go down into the remarkable caldera of the well-known Ngorongoro Crater. On this day in particular it pays to begin your game drive early, when there are many animals and few tourists. As you descend into the crater, the sight of hovering clouds and the many animals around you will give you goosebumps. Coyotes, hyenas, buffaloes, wildebeests, gazelles and many other animals live here, and you are almost certain to see all of them.

blocks.orig: Fly into the mind-blowing beautiful Serengeti National Park for the epitome of safari. See the infamous Big Five in all their glory, and, in certain months, wildebeests running by the thousands in the Great Migration. And even without that; this is big-cat-paradise with prides of lions on kopjes, cheetahs in the long, yellow grass, and leopards in trees. You arrive in time for an amazing afternoon game drive into the sunset.
blocks.html: You fly into the stunning Serengeti National Park, the very essence of a safari. Here you can see the famous Big Five in full splendour and, in certain months, thousands of wildebeests on the move during the Great Migration. Even without the migration, this is a paradise for big cats: prides of lions on kopjes, cheetahs in the long yellow grass and leopards in the trees. You get there in time for a superb afternoon game drive as the sun goes down.

blocks.orig: Anything you can think of when you picture a luxurious safari, you will surely find in Serengeti National Park. Not only the Big Five, the famous Great Migration, and a multitude of big cats, but also rarer species such as the gerenuk or the wild dog, and did we mention the plus 500 species of birds? In between, you naturally spot antelopes, giraffes, elephants, zebras, hippos, and many more animals. Make sure to wake up at sunrise for an epic balloon safari...!
blocks.html: Whatever you imagine when you think of a luxury safari, you will find it in Serengeti National Park. Besides the Big Five, the famous Great Migration and many big cats, there are also rarer species such as the gerenuk and the wild dog, plus more than 500 bird species. Along the way you will of course see antelopes, giraffes, elephants, zebras, hippos and plenty of other animals. Be sure to get up at sunrise for an unforgettable balloon safari!

blocks.orig: A balloon safari in the iconic Serengeti National Park will make your Tanzania safari a memorable experience. You rise at sunrise and gently fly over the endless plains of the Serengeti. The hot air balloon floats at treetop height above the baobabs and acacias so that you can see the animals nearby. Watching the wildlife below from your balloon is a fascinating and peaceful experience that comes with breathtaking panoramic views.
blocks.html: Taking a balloon safari over the iconic Serengeti National Park turns your Tanzania safari into an experience to remember. You go up at sunrise and drift slowly across the vast Serengeti plains. The balloon glides at treetop height over the baobabs and acacias, so you can see the animals close by. Looking down on the wildlife from the balloon is a captivating and calm experience, with stunning views all around.

blocks.orig: Today you fly to the spice island of Zanzibar. Our guide picks you up at the airport and takes you to your hotel. Over the next few days, you can discover white sandy beaches, crystal-clear turquoise waters and vibrant coral reefs. Into culture? Then head to Stone Town and dive into the history of this fascinating little town. Food lovers can also visit the spice plantations and discover the diverse flavours of the delicious local cuisine. A tropical paradise awaits you!
blocks.html: Today you take a flight to Zanzibar, the spice island. Our guide meets you at the airport and drives you to your hotel. In the days that follow you can explore white sandy beaches, clear turquoise water and colourful coral reefs. Interested in culture? Go to Stone Town and learn about the history of this fascinating small town. If you love food, you can also visit the spice plantations and taste the varied flavours of the excellent local cuisine. A tropical paradise is waiting for you!

blocks.orig: From the beautiful yellows of the Tanzanian savannah, you fly to the most fabulous white beaches of... Zanzibar! Get pampered by a fantastic staff in a luxurious five-star all-inclusive resort on the coast, and spend your days swimming, surfing, or just chillin' in a hammock with a cocktail in hand. Expect your own piece of paradise with kilometers of palm-fringed beaches, wooden dhows on the horizon, and an ocean so blue you need sunglasses to even look at it…!
blocks.html: You leave the lovely yellow tones of the Tanzanian savannah behind and fly to the beautiful white beaches of... Zanzibar! A wonderful team looks after you at a luxurious five-star all-inclusive resort on the coast, and you fill your days with swimming, surfing or simply relaxing in a hammock with a cocktail. Your own piece of paradise awaits, with kilometres of beaches lined with palms, wooden dhows on the horizon and an ocean so blue you will want sunglasses just to look at it!

blocks.orig: The last day! Depending on your flight time, you can relax on the beach or explore the island just a little bit more. Then, make your way to Zanzibar International Airport in time for your flight home. Having second thoughts? It's also possible to extend your holiday to another paradise island, such as Mnemba, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can enjoy the beach or see a little more of the island. After that you travel to Zanzibar International Airport to catch your flight home. Not ready to leave yet? You can also extend your holiday on another paradise island, such as Mnemba, Pemba or Mafia!
